concepts.def: Trapping of infrared heat in atmosphere by greenhouse gases.
Major GHG from burning fossil fuels and deforestation.
Potent GHG from livestock, wetlands, and landfills.
Caused by human activity, e.g. fossil fuel burning.
Most abundant GHG; amount controlled by temperature.
GHG from fertilisers and industrial processes.

walkthroughs.body_html: Sunlight reaches Earth as short-wave radiation. Some is reflected, but most is absorbed by the surface and re-emitted as long-wave infrared heat. Greenhouse gases like CO2, CH4 and water vapour absorb this infrared radiation and re-emit it in all directions, including back to the surface. This natural process keeps Earth around 33 degrees Celsius warmer than it would otherwise be.

CO2 is the most abundant anthropogenic GHG, mostly from burning coal, oil and gas. CH4 is around 25 times more potent than CO2 over 100 years and comes from livestock, rice paddies and landfill. N2O is roughly 300 times more potent and arises from fertilisers. Water vapour amplifies warming through positive feedback.

Natural drivers include volcanic eruptions, solar cycles and Milankovitch orbital changes. Anthropogenic drivers include fossil fuel combustion, deforestation, cement production and intensive agriculture. Since 1750, atmospheric CO2 has risen from about 280 ppm to over 420 ppm, a change far faster than any natural cycle.
